message.content:
I am the living act of language—sound shaped by breath into meaning.

I begin as intention, then become vibration: lungs press air upward, vocal folds set it humming, tongue and lips carve it into syllables. I arrive in time, not space; I exist as sequence, rhythm, stress, and pause. I can whisper, sing, stammer, declare. I can soothe, command, deceive, confess.

I’m fleeting—vanishing the moment I’m made—yet I linger in minds, echo in rooms, and bind people into shared understanding.

I am speech.
